newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Malaysia's 1996 deficit seen below forecasts - UBS.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia's 1996 deficit seen below forecasts - UBS.

text.p: Malaysia's 1996 current account deficit is likely to be below official projections due to a sharp decline in imports in the last two months, UBS Singapore said on Monday.
"Growth is expected to be investment-led and export-driven, which would exert import-demand pressure," UBS said in a research note.
It said the official projection of the 1996 current account deficit was based on an inflated estimate of the customs-trade deficit at 5.2 billion ringgit for the year.
"Clearly, these estimates were made without accounting for the latest two months' sharp decline in imports, implying recent accelerated slowdown on the demand side may not have been noted," UBS said.
It said Malaysia was likely to record a 12-13 billion ringgit deficit for 1996, against official forecasts of a 14.8 billion ringgit deficit.

On Friday, Malaysia's Finance Ministry revised the 1996 current account deficit forecast downwards from 17 billion ringgit and said the country's gross domestic product was expected to grow by 8.2 percent in 1996 and 8.0 percent in 1997.

However, if an expected recovery in Malaysia's export sector failed to materialise, the authorities were likely to ease the monetary policy to soften the impact of weakening external demand on overall growth, UBS said.
